comment: The governance principles give necessary weight to underserved communities, but they do not explicitly require frontline clinical, clinical-informatics or patient-safety expertise in decisions that can affect care delivery. A deployment could therefore meet the stated representation principle while clinically consequential architecture decisions are made without those who understand workflow hazards, service constraints and patient-safety consequences.

public.text: The governance principles give necessary weight to underserved communities, but they do not explicitly require frontline clinical, clinical-informatics or patient-safety expertise in decisions that can affect care delivery. A deployment could therefore meet the stated representation principle while clinically consequential architecture decisions are made without those who understand workflow hazards, service constraints and patient-safety consequences.
public.suggestedRevision: Add a governance principle on clinical and service accountability: governance bodies should include frontline clinical, clinical-informatics, patient-safety and service-user expertise, with defined decision rights for safety-relevant architecture, data and workflow decisions. Representation should be proportionate to the clinical consequences of the decision, not merely advisory.
